content.title: About
content.content: Waffle is a light, crisp baked good made from a batter of flour, eggs, milk and sugar. Waffles are often served with tea or coffee and can be enjoyed as a snack or used in desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Waffles originated in medieval Europe and were originally cooked in special iron presses.
There are more than 30 types of waffle batters, including Belgian, American and Liege waffles.
Waffles are a common quick and nutritious snack in school cafeterias.
Traditional Belgian waffles have deeper pockets that hold syrup and whipped cream.
Waffles can be sweet or savory depending on the added ingredients.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Waffles provide quickly digestible carbs that give energy for studying and physical activity.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Thanks to eggs and milk, waffles supply a modest amount of both animal and plant protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole‑grain batter is enriched with B1, B2 and niacin, important for the nervous system.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Milk in the batter provides calcium needed for bone growth in children.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The soft texture makes waffles convenient for younger children.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweet waffles can contain high amounts of sugar, increasing the risk of cavities and excess weight.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional waffles are made with wheat flour, which can be problematic for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Cooking in oil high in trans fats can make waffles less healthy.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Waffles are relatively calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Waffles can be enjoyed hot with honey, jam, butter or fresh fruit. They are also used in desserts—as a base for cakes, parfaits and ice‑cream toppings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store waffles in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator up to a week or freeze up to 2 months.
